status_summary: On 2025-04-23 Interior announced emergency permitting procedures for energy and critical minerals projects under existing NEPA, Endangered Species Act and historic preservation emergency provisions, targeting about 14 days for reviews that would otherwise need an environmental assessment and about 28 days for those needing an environmental impact statement. On 2026-03-17 BLM issued a memorandum on deficiency extensions for drilling permit applications with weekly reporting of pending applications. BLM data show the average federal and Indian drilling permit took 283 days in fiscal year 2025, and no requirement that regional offices match state average permit times was found.

timeline.event: Interior announced emergency permitting procedures for energy and minerals projects with target timeframes of about 14 days (environmental assessments) and about 28 days (environmental impact statements).
BLM issued Instruction Memorandum 2026-013 on deficiency extension requests when processing applications for permit to drill, with weekly reporting of pending applications.

title: Match state average times for Interior rights-of-way and drilling permits
uncertainties: In review on 2026-10-18 the Interior release of 2025-04-23 was re-read: it covers energy and critical minerals projects, sets review targets of about 14 days for environmental assessments and about 28 days for environmental impact statements, does not mention drilling permits or rights-of-way specifically, and makes no comparison to state timelines. BLM Instruction Memorandum 2026-013 was re-read: signed 2026-03-17, posted 2026-03-18, effective on issuance through 2029-09-30, it allows multiple extensions of the 45-day deficiency period, asks field offices to process deficiency-free applications first and orders weekly reporting of pending applications; it sets no overall processing target and no state comparison and does not cover rights-of-way. The BLM processing-time table covers federal and Indian drilling permits only; its date is a month-only date taken from the file path. A Federal Register API query of BLM permit-to-drill documents through 2026-10-18 found no state-average benchmark requirement; a review variant on right-of-way processing time returned two BLM proposed rules (Oil and Gas Leasing, 2026-06-24, and the NPR-A production site rule, 2026-09-08), seen only through search excerpts and abstracts, so any processing deadlines in them were not read. Public Law 119-21 permitting sections and 2025 secretarial orders were not read. The stage rests partly on the absence of a requirement.
